2026-10-12T16:46:00Z_CORRECTION_TTMI_NUL.finding:
CORRECTION to the 16:16 journal entry's theory (ABSTAIN-vs-VETO_BLIND) -- continued tracing found I had the persistence layer wrong. Read cortex-gate.ts's cortexEntryContextFor (the actual assessment->persisted-blob converter, which I hadn't located last cycle) in full: `if (assessment.abstained) return {abstained:true, reason: assessment.reason}` -- a TRUE ABSTAIN persists as a REAL non-null object with a reason string, NOT null. The ONLY path that returns bare `null` is `if (assessment == null) return null` with its own comment: 'Cortex never ran (refresh lane) -- no blob, never a fake one.' So TTMI's persisted cortex:null means the `s.cortex` JS variable was literally null/undefined at persist time -- NOT that evaluateCortexForCommit ran and returned ABSTAIN. This is a DIFFERENT, more specific question than previously framed.

evaluateCortexForCommit's own signature/implementation NEVER returns null (always a real ZeroDteCortexAssessment object, confirmed via its try/catch which also returns a real ABSTAIN object on any thrown error) -- and applyCortexVetoDwell/applyCortexCommitRelief are BOTH typed to return non-nullable ZeroDteCortexAssessment too. So for s.cortex to end up as bare null after scan.ts's three-line sequence (evaluate -> dwell -> relief), either (a) TTMI's commit never actually went through this exact scan.ts loop at all (no other call site of evaluateCortexForCommit exists repo-wide -- confirmed via grep, so this would mean a different commit mechanism entirely that I haven't located), or (b) the 'refresh lane' comment's scenario applies: a LATER re-persist of entry_context (e.g. when the thesis_break exit wrote its own exit block onto the row) called cortexEntryContextFor(null, ...) because that refresh code path intentionally never re-evaluates Cortex and passes null rather than carrying the ORIGINAL commit-time cortex value forward -- which would mean the original real cortex blob from commit-time was DESTROYED/overwritten on exit, a DATA-LOSS bug distinct from any pre-commit firewall question. Note this would NOT be universal: IONQ/QQQ/SPXW/TSLA/PENG all exited today too and ALL retained real cortex blobs post-exit, so if (b) is right there's something ELSE distinguishing TTMI's refresh path specifically (discovery_origin BREAKOUT? play_type? the exact exit reason?) -- not yet identified.

Still NOT a confirmed bug -- genuinely could not settle (a) vs (b) vs a third explanation from static reading alone within this cycle's scope. Sharper framing for the next follow-up (mine or Cursor's): grep for every OTHER caller of cortexEntryContextFor (not just evaluateCortexForCommit) to find the refresh-lane call site and check whether it threads the row's EXISTING persisted cortex through or always passes null.

Found cortexEntryContextFor's one real call site: scan.ts:1831-1834, inside `eligible.map(...)` where `eligible = [...committedFresh, ...refresh]`. Checked whether TTMI could have gone through the `refresh` lane (pre-existing rows re-persisted without re-running Cortex, built from board.ts's generic setup object which defaults cortex:null) rather than `committedFresh` -- it could NOT: `refresh = setups.filter(s => existing.has(ticker))`, and TTMI was a genuinely NEW ticker this session, so it must have come through `freshCandidates` -> `committedFresh`, the SAME gate+cortex loop (scan.ts ~1250-1320) as every other fresh commit today. CONCLUDING this round of static tracing here -- 3 cycles in, the evidence keeps pointing back to 'null at the moment of commit despite failClosedOnVetoBlind:true routing through the exact same loop as every successful play today', but I cannot fully rule out either a subtle object-reference loss between committedFresh and the eligible.map persist step, or a narrow legitimate code path I still haven't located, from static reading alone. Keeping this OPEN in the journal rather than re-deriving from scratch next time; not spending further cycles on unaided static tracing unless a 2nd TTMI-shaped instance (fresh commit + persisted cortex:null) shows up, which would be worth a focused live-capture attempt.

open_findings.summary: The recurring "board.ledger lags /record" pattern (previously observed 3x this week: CIFR/SPCH, CRDO/HOOD, CORZ -- noted as "not yet investigated as a bug, would need a 4th+ occurrence") now has a 4th, well-evidenced instance with a real member-facing consequence: CMPS closed via thesis_break:gex-walls at -27.63% (2026-09-17T16:02:29Z, full narrative correctly persisted to entry_context.exit per GET /record). But GET /board kept showing status=CLOSED with closed_reason="time_stop" and exit_reason=null/exit_detail=null across THREE separate fresh polls spanning ~20 minutes (as_of timestamps up to 16:05:41Z, i.e. AFTER the real exit) -- not a few-seconds race, a sustained wrong label. A member reading the live board during that window would see "time_stop" (implying the play simply ran the clock to 3:50pm ET) when the real story was an early, structural thesis-break veto at ~12:02 ET -- a materially different and misleading explanation of why their position closed. Eventually self-corrected (confirmed on a later poll) with no data loss -- the underlying DB row was always correct, only the served board payload was stale/wrong for an extended window.
open_findings.root_cause_hypothesis_not_db_confirmed: Traced two candidate layers, not fully confirmed without direct Postgres access (blocked in this sandbox): (1) src/lib/platform/zerodte-service.ts:494-499 `boardClosedReason` fallback is `engineExitCategory ?? "time_stop"` -- UNCONDITIONAL, not gated on whether nowEtMinutes is actually near/past PLAN_RULES.time_stop_et_minutes (15:50 ET). This is a real logic defect independent of any timing race: ANY row whose engineExitCategory cannot be derived (missing/stale entry_context.exit, unmapped reason) gets mislabeled "time_stop" specifically, regardless of actual time of day -- CMPS closed at ~12:02 ET, nowhere near the real time-stop threshold, yet got that exact label. (2) src/lib/zerodte/scan.ts syncLedgerLiveState (~line 2722-2728): the in-memory `nextRow` returned after an exit-engine EXIT is `{...r, status, last_mark, peak_premium, trough_premium}` -- it does NOT merge in the entry_context that evaluateLedgerRowExit just wrote to Postgres via stampZeroDteExitContext (exit-sync.ts:515-518, a separate best-effort DB write). So the SAME request/tick that closes a play via the exit engine would always render that build with a stale entry_context (no .exit) -- self-correcting only once a LATER buildZeroDteBoardPayload does a fresh readZeroDteLedgerChecked() DB read that picks up the by-then-persisted stamp. Does not fully explain why THIS instance took ~20 minutes across 3 distinct polls when the warm cron runs ~every 5 min -- that gap is the part still needing DB-side confirmation (e.g. whether readZeroDteLedgerChecked is itself served from a cache layer this sandbox cannot inspect, or whether some other condition kept re-selecting the stale row).
open_findings.why_not_fixed_yet: The (1) fallback-gating fix (only label "time_stop" when nowEtMinutes is genuinely near/past the threshold) is narrative-only and low-risk, similar in shape to the flat_theta_bleed trough-narrative fix shipped this session (PR #5139) -- but shipping it without nailing WHY the propagation gap ran ~20min (vs the "a few minutes" seen in the 3 prior instances) risks fixing the visible symptom while leaving a real, larger caching/staleness bug unexplained. Root-causing (2) fully needs either DB access (blocked here) or CloudWatch logs for the zerodte-warm cron cadence around this window -- neither available from this sandbox. Per escalation policy: ambiguous/architecturally-relevant, holding for direction rather than shipping a partial fix.
